nodes.title: The rank-one geometric Hom lattice
nodes.statement: Let K=k(U) with k algebraically closed of characteristic zero. For a nonisotrivial elliptic curve E/K, End(E over an algebraic closure of K)=Z. If E′ is geometrically isogenous to E, then Hom(E,E′ over that algebraic closure) is a free rank-one Z-module. A primitive generator f has Galois conjugates σ(f)=χ(σ)f for a continuous character χ:G_K→{±1}. If some geometric isogeny has degree prime to p, then p∤deg f.
proofSteps: Import finite generation and torsion-freeness of Hom and degree scaling. Once geometric End(E)=Z, choose any geometric isogeny h:E→E′. Composition g↦h∨∘g injects Hom(E,E′) into End(E): a homomorphism into the finite kernel of h∨ is zero because its source is connected. Its image contains the nonzero h∨h=[deg h], so this free Hom module has rank exactly one. No unproved rational-Hom-dimension assertion is imported.

Spread any extra endomorphism and its defining equations to a finite cover of a finite-type model. Over C its locally constant action on the lattice, together with the period description, forces a fixed imaginary-quadratic period and hence constant j. Nonconstancy survives the faithfully flat spread, giving the contradiction.

Galois acts on a free rank-one lattice by its two units. A generator and its negative are defined over a finite extension, so the character is continuous. If h=a f then deg h=a²deg f, which gives the prime-to-p assertion.
acceptance: Constant-j CM curves are excluded: their geometric endomorphism ring need not be Z.
The primitive generator need not be the particular cyclic isogeny furnished by a Hecke component.

sources.match: Theorem 1 concludes that the families are isogenous; passing from a geometric isogeny to one over k(U) uses the structure of the geometric Hom group of a nonisotrivial elliptic curve, which the source does not discuss. The node is that standard fact, proved here.

nodes.title: Hecke containment gives a geometric prime-to-p isogeny
nodes.statement: If the classifying map f_Ψ is contained in H_m with p∤m, then over an algebraic closure of K=k(U) there is a cyclic isogeny f:E→E′ of degree m whose restriction to p-torsion is a scalar multiple of the given isomorphism: f[p]=λΨ for some λ∈F_p^×. Consequently the primitive generator of the geometric Hom lattice has degree prime to p.
proofSteps: The finite normalized cyclic correspondence surjects onto H_m. Lift the geometric generic point of the image of U to it: this gives framed curves (E₁,φ₁),(E₂,φ₂) and a cyclic isogeny f₀:E₁→E₂ of degree m with f₀[p]φ₁ proportional to φ₂, together with isomorphisms a:E→E₁ and b:E′→E₂ identifying the triple (E,E′,[Ψ]) with (E₁,E₂,[φ₂φ₁⁻¹]).
Put f=b⁻¹f₀a. It is cyclic of degree m and f[p]=λΨ for a scalar λ, because both sides induce the same projective map E[p]→E′[p]. Automorphisms of the nonisotrivial curves are ±1 and only change λ.
The lift is defined over a finite extension of K; its descent to K is GF.9/actual-linear-descent. Degree scaling in the rank-one Hom lattice gives the statement about the primitive generator.
acceptance: For E′=E and Ψ=id the containment is in H₁ and f=id, λ=1.
For E′=E/K with K a cyclic subgroup of order m prime to p and Ψ=π_K[p], the containment is in H_m and f=π_K, λ=1.

sources.match: §2.5 defines T_m by cyclic isogenies compatible with the frames, so a point of Z(p) on H_m comes from such an isogeny; Theorem 1 uses this to pass from Theorem 3 to isogenies. The node records what Hecke containment gives over an algebraic closure of k(U), including the scalar relation with Ψ.

nodes.title: Actual p-torsion removes the isogeny twist
nodes.statement: Let K=k(U) with k algebraically closed of characteristic zero, p an odd prime, E/K nonisotrivial, and Ψ:E[p]≃E′[p] an actual G_K-equivariant F_p-linear isomorphism. If an isogeny f:E→E′ defined over an algebraic closure of K satisfies f[p]=λΨ for some λ∈F_p^× (as Hecke containment provides), then f is defined over K, so E and E′ are K-isogenous. No hypothesis on the image of the p-torsion representation is needed.
proofSteps: For σ∈G_K the conjugate isogeny satisfies σ(f)[p]=σ∘(λΨ)∘σ⁻¹=λΨ=f[p], because Ψ is G_K-equivariant and λ is a scalar.
By the rank-one geometric Hom lattice, σ(f)=χ(σ)f with χ(σ)=±1. Since f[p] is invertible and p is odd, χ(σ)f[p]=f[p] forces χ(σ)=1.

Galois descent of morphisms descends f to K. The projective class of Ψ alone would not suffice: for a nontrivial quadratic twist E′=E^χ the geometric isomorphism f satisfies σ(f)=χ(σ)f, so f[p] is not a scalar multiple of any G_K-equivariant isomorphism, and the full-image argument of GF.8/no-quadratic-self-twist is not needed on this route.
acceptance: For a generic nonisotrivial E over C(t), a nontrivial quadratic twist has the same projective p-torsion for odd p and is not C(t)-isogenous to E.
With E′=E, Ψ=[−1] and f=id one has f[p]=−Ψ, a scalar multiple, and f descends, as it must.

sources.match: Theorem 1 asserts an isogeny of families over U, while Hecke containment provides one over an algebraic closure of k(U); the source does not write the descent. The node supplies it from the actual torsion isomorphism.

nodes.title: Extend the generic isogeny over the original open curve
nodes.statement: For elliptic schemes E,E′ over a smooth connected characteristic-zero curve U, every isogeny of their generic fibres extends uniquely to an isogeny E→E′ over U. The extension is a finite locally free surjective group morphism. This asserts an isogeny over U, not merely over a finite cover or an extension of its function field.
proofSteps: A smooth curve is a Dedekind base. By the imported Néron mapping property, the good-reduction abelian schemes E and E′ are their generic fibres’ Néron models; extend the isogeny and its dual.
Extend the two identities involving multiplication by its degree using uniqueness on the generic fibre. The kernel lies in the finite étale degree-torsion because the characteristic is zero.
Use the abelian-scheme finite-kernel/isogeny criterion to obtain finite local freeness and surjectivity, preserving group structure by uniqueness.
acceptance: A rational map between arbitrary proper models does not suffice; the group-scheme/Néron property is the precise input.
Removing more points of U commutes with the unique extension.

sources.match: BLR §1.2 Proposition 8 states that an abelian scheme over a Dedekind scheme is the Néron model of its generic fibre, so morphisms from the generic fibre of a smooth scheme extend uniquely; §1.4 Proposition 2 states that a smooth proper extension of an abelian variety over a connected Dedekind scheme is an abelian scheme, hence its Néron model. The node applies these to the generic isogeny and its dual.

nodes.title: Uniform rigidity over any characteristic-zero k
nodes.statement: The geometric-rigidity threshold M_N^geom works unchanged for every algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k: for p>M_N^geom, every nonconstant map to Z(p) from a smooth connected k-curve of gonality <N has image in an irreducible component of some H_m with p∤m, and for the classifying map of an actual torsion isomorphism the cyclic isogeny with f[p]=λΨ of GF.9/geometric-prime-to-p-isogeny exists over an algebraic closure of k(U). The quantifiers are uniform in k, the curves and the maps; no embedding of all of k into C is required.
proofSteps: Descend the proper base, the open subset, the map to Z(p), a degree-n pencil with n<N, and any finite étale torsion data to one finitely generated subfield k₀⊂k. Preserve smoothness, nonconstant j and nonconstancy of the map after enlarging k₀.

Embed k₀ in C and apply the complex theorem after algebraic closure. Containment in a particular closed Hecke locus H_m is equality of a pulled-back ideal with zero, hence descends by faithful flatness to the model over an algebraic closure of k₀ and then extends to k. Only the model field, rather than k itself, is embedded.

After the closed Hecke containment descends, lift its geometric generic point through the finite cyclic correspondence over k itself. This supplies the cyclic isogeny with f[p]=λΨ without asserting that arbitrary analytic homomorphisms descend.
acceptance: A field k of cardinality greater than that of C is permitted; only a finitely generated field is embedded.
Spread the pencil and the actual isomorphism, rather than a numerical claim about gonality or a semisimplified representation.

sources.match: Theorem 1 is stated over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, while §2.1 restricts all schemes to the complex numbers and §§3–7 argue analytically. The node supplies the passage from C to an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, which the source leaves implicit.

nodes.title: Full linear monodromy over any characteristic-zero k
nodes.statement: For every algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, every integer N>0, every smooth connected k-curve U with gon(U)<N and every nonisotrivial elliptic scheme E/U, the actual p-torsion monodromy image is SL₂(F_p) for every prime p>max(5,800N/7), after a choice of basis with fixed Weil pairing.
proofSteps: Descend U, a degree-n pencil with n<N, E and a geometric base point to a finitely generated subfield k₀⊂k, preserving smoothness, connectedness and nonconstant j; embed k₀ in C.

Apply GF.8/full-linear-monodromy over C. Invariance of the geometric finite étale fundamental group under algebraically closed characteristic-zero extension identifies the actual monodromy images; equivalently every connected finite frame torsor stays connected. The descended pencil gives gonality at most n; the exact minimum need not be preserved.
acceptance: The constant-j case is excluded, as over C.
This is a theorem of the roadmap in its own right; the descent of isogenies in GF.9 does not use it.

sources.locator: Remark after Theorem 2 and footnote 3, p. 710
sources.match: Page 710 states surjectivity onto SL₂(F_p) for large p as a remark over C, and Theorem 1 is stated over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The node is the surjectivity statement over such a field, obtained by spreading out; the source does not write this step.

nodes.title: Geometric Frey–Mazur over the original base
nodes.statement: For every integer N>0 there exists M_N such that, for every algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, prime p>M_N, smooth connected quasiprojective k-curve U with gon(U)<N, and nonisotrivial elliptic schemes E,E′/U, an actual isomorphism E[p]≃E′[p] of finite étale F_p-module schemes implies an isogeny E→E′ over U. One may take any M_N≥max(M_N^geom,5); no bound on the image of the torsion representation is used. There is no claimed explicit numerical threshold.
proofSteps: Form the nonconstant classifying map, extend it to the smooth proper base and apply uniform geometric rigidity. The image lies on H_m for some p∤m, and the Hecke lift gives a geometric cyclic isogeny f with f[p]=λΨ.
Apply actual-linear descent to f to obtain an isogeny over K=k(U).
Extend it uniquely over the original U using the good-reduction Néron models. All thresholds depend only on N.
acceptance: The output is defined over U, without a finite étale replacement of the base.
The theorem assumes actual F_p-local systems and both families are nonisotrivial; it makes no assertion in positive characteristic or over Q at p>17.

sources.match: Theorem 1 states that for p>M_N nonisotrivial elliptic curves over a smooth quasiprojective curve of gonality <N over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero are classified up to isogeny by their p-torsion local system. The node states it with the isogeny over U.

nodes.title: Equivalent geometric function-field formulation
nodes.statement: Equivalently, for every N>0 there is M_N such that for K=k(B), k algebraically closed of characteristic zero, B a smooth proper connected curve of gonality <N, and nonisotrivial elliptic curves E,E′/K, an actual G_K-equivariant F_p-linear isomorphism E[p]≃E′[p] for prime p>M_N implies a K-isogeny. Restricting to a common good-reduction open and extending its finite étale torsion data gives the family statement; taking generic fibres gives the converse.
proofSteps: An elliptic curve and a morphism of finite étale torsion group schemes spread over a common nonempty good-reduction open. Shrink finitely many points to make the two inverse torsion morphisms defined.
The smooth proper model and hence gonality do not change under restriction to this open. Apply the family theorem and pass to the generic fibre.
Conversely the function-field theorem followed by the extension theorem yields the original-base assertion.
acceptance: Ramification at the finitely many omitted bad-reduction points is allowed in the G_K representation.
No equality of semisimplified Galois representations is substituted for the actual isomorphism.

sources.match: Theorem 2 restates Theorem 1 for nonisotrivial elliptic curves over k(B), B smooth projective of gonality <N, classified up to isogeny by their p-torsion Galois representations for p>M_N. The node is Theorem 2 with an actual Galois-equivariant isomorphism.

nodes.title: Bounded-genus rigidity with an enlarged threshold
nodes.statement: For each integer N>0 there exists P_N such that every map from a smooth connected curve whose proper model has genus g<N to Z(p), for prime p>P_N, has image either a point or a Hecke curve. One may choose P_N=M_(N+1)^geom, using gon(B)≤g+1≤N<N+1. The same enlargement gives the actual-torsion isogeny theorem for nonisotrivial families on those bases.
proofSteps: Import the Riemann–Roch gonality bound; no new Riemann–Roch theory is planned here.
Handle constant maps separately and apply geometric rigidity to a nonconstant map. Apply the family theorem to the torsion consequence.
acceptance: The strict gonality inequality is met by N+1, even when gon(B)=N.

sources.match: Corollary 30 states that for p>M_N every curve of genus <N on Z(p) is a Hecke curve, deduced from Theorem 29 through the bound gon(B)≤g(B)+1 recalled on p. 740. The node is Corollary 30 with the enlarged threshold made explicit.

nodes.title: Rational and elliptic curves are Hecke
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large prime p, every integral curve on Z(p) whose normalization has genus zero or one is a Hecke curve. A common threshold is M_3^geom: a rational normalization has gonality 1 and a genus-one normalization over an algebraically closed field has gonality 2.
proofSteps: Apply the imported genus-zero and genus-one pencil bounds to the normalization of the curve.
The normalization map is nonconstant, so geometric rigidity places its image in an irreducible component of a Hecke locus. Equal dimensions give equality of integral curves.
acceptance: A singular rational curve is tested by its normalization, not its arithmetic genus.
A constant map from an elliptic curve does not produce an integral elliptic image curve.

sources.match: Corollary 31 states that for large p every rational or elliptic curve in Z(p) is a Hecke curve, answering a question of Kani and Schanz. The node is Corollary 31 for integral curves whose normalization has genus 0 or 1.

nodes.title: The resolution and its known curve set
nodes.statement: Resolve the isolated cyclic quotient singularities of a determinant component of Z(p). At a CM or singular-bicusp point the local action is 1/n(1,a), n∈{2,3,p}, gcd(a,n)=1, with a determined by the tangent characters; import its Hirzebruch–Jung resolution. On the resulting smooth projective surface Z̃(p), define the known curves to be all exceptional components and all strict transforms of Hecke curves. The resolution is an application of the owning surface interface, not a new general resolution theory.
proofSteps: Read the stabilizer characters from the exact branch-locus theorem. Nonidentity inertia fixes neither individual tangent direction, so both weights are units modulo n.
Apply the supplied cyclic-quotient resolution and intersection formulas. Its exceptional chains are rational curves; take strict transforms of each Hecke curve using proper birational transforms.
The construction is algebraic in characteristic zero and commutes with the supplied base changes; the metric is not part of the surface carrier.
acceptance: A 1/n(1,a) point resolves to a chain with self-intersections −b_i from the continued fraction n/a=b₁−1/(b₂−…): 1/3(1,1) gives one (−3)-curve, 1/3(1,2) two (−2)-curves, and 1/p(1,p−1) a chain of p−1 (−2)-curves.

sources.match: That paragraph describes the cyclic quotient singularities of Z(p), locally C² modulo Z/n acting by (ζz,ζ^a w) with n=2 or 3 at CM points and n=p at singular bicusps, and their minimal resolution by chains of smooth rational curves governed by the continued fraction of n/a. The node defines the resolution Z̃(p) and its known curves.

nodes.title: Every rational curve on the resolution is known
nodes.statement: For prime p>M_3^geom, every integral rational curve on Z̃(p) is either an exceptional component or the strict transform of a Hecke curve. In particular every initial (−1)-curve belongs to the known set.
proofSteps: If the curve is not exceptional, its image in Z(p) is an integral curve with the same normalization function field. Its normalization is rational.
Apply the rational-curve consequence and take the unique strict transform. Exceptional fibres contain exactly the listed irreducible components.
acceptance: An exceptional component maps to a point of Z(p) and a strict transform maps birationally onto its Hecke curve; for p>M₃^geom no rational curve of a third kind exists.

sources.match: The one-line proof of Corollary 32 uses Corollary 30 to say that every rational curve on Z̃(p) is exceptional or the strict transform of a Hecke curve. The node is that statement.

nodes.title: A minimal model obtained by contracting known curves
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large prime p, a smooth minimal model of each component of Z(p) can be obtained from Z̃(p) by finitely many contractions of smooth rational (−1)-curves. At every step, the contracted curve is the image of a known rational curve on the original resolution. Thus the required contractions are supported on the known Hecke and exceptional curves. The assertion does not identify every Hecke curve as contractible and does not say each subsequent centre was a (−1)-curve on the original surface.
proofSteps: Import Castelnuovo contraction and termination by strict decrease of the Picard number, from the proposed surface-contraction extension. If no (−1)-curve remains, this is the surface-minimality conclusion.

Under the inverse sequence of blowups, the strict transform of each subsequent contracted smooth rational curve is still an integral rational curve on the original resolution. Apply the classification of known rational curves there.
Record intersection numbers after each contraction using the supplied formula. Existence of some smooth minimal model is enough; no general-type classification or uniqueness theorem is used.
acceptance: A curve of self-intersection −2 is not contractible to a smooth point by the (−1)-curve theorem.
A subsequent (−1)-curve may have self-intersection below −1 on Z̃; update intersections after each preceding contraction.

sources.match: Corollary 32 states that for large p the minimal model of Z(p) is obtained from Z̃(p) by blowing down strict transforms of Hecke curves and curves contracted by Z̃(p)→Z(p), answering a conjecture of Hermann. The node keeps this as an existence statement for a smooth minimal model, without the uniqueness that the source takes from general type.

For a compact quotient require R<ρ_X and lift the ball. This is additional to the existing point-multiplicity lower bound, not a consequence of the diagonal-tube theorem. On the normalization put u=log max_i|z_i|², s_t=log tanh²(t/2), h(s)=−log(1−exp(s)), v=Σ_i h(log|z_i|²), and N(s)=∫_{u<s}dd^c u. For any nonconstant finite map of smooth proper connected algebraic curves B→D over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, gon(D)≤gon(B). Proof: push a pencil’s fibre divisors to D, use the norm of ratios for linear equivalence, show the family varies, remove base points and take a pencil of degree at most the original. No existing HV.6 node states this domination lemma.

Elementary trigonometry of the curvature −1 half-plane, which the upstream FuchsianOrbifolds roadmap does not state: a hyperbolic element of PSL₂(R) with |tr|>2 has translation length 2arcosh(|tr|/2), attained on its axis; the second law of cosines for a geodesic triangle with angles α,β,γ; and, for a rotation by angle θ about a point at distance d, the displacement D satisfies sinh(D/2)=sinh d·|sin(θ/2)|.

Projective finite quotients and the cycle morphism. The atlas node SF.1/finite-group-quotient gives the scheme quotient, its orbit fibres and universal property; the upstream SchemeAndStackFoundations README §1.17 (finiteGroupQuotient_projective) states projectivity of Y/Γ for Y projective over a Noetherian base, with the invariant norm polarization M=⊗γ*L and flat base change, but no atlas node states it yet. Still absent everywhere: étaleness of Y→Y/Γ over the image of the free locus when the action is not free, and the relative cycle (norm) morphism sending a finite flat family of degree-n subschemes of a projective surface Z to SymⁿZ=Zⁿ/S_n, with fibre multiplicities.

In the named setting of projective characteristic-zero surfaces: resolve cyclic quotient charts 1/n(1,a), with Hirzebruch–Jung chains, rational exceptional components and strict transforms; provide Castelnuovo contraction of smooth rational (−1)-curves to smooth projective surfaces and termination by decreasing Picard number. Only the arithmetic-surface contraction of StableReduction Layer 4 and SF.4/bertini-smoothness (smoothness of a general section, without connectedness) exist now. No existing node supplies the resolution or the contraction; a dedicated surface-contraction Part II is proposed in restructure.

On a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field: the self-intersection numbers of the Hirzebruch–Jung chain resolving a 1/n(1,a) point, read from the continued fraction of n/a; and the update C_new²=C_old²+(C_old·E)² for the image of a curve under contraction of a smooth rational (−1)-curve E. Degrees, flat pullback, proper pushforward and the projection formula are cited from the existing SF.5 nodes.
Uses §2C as stated: for an isogeny φ:E→E′ of elliptic curves of constant degree n over a base, the factorisation dual satisfies φ̂∘φ=[n]_E and φ∘φ̂=[n]_{E′}.

Smooth proper models of one-variable function fields over an algebraically closed field, finite normalization, extension of a morphism from a smooth curve to a proper target across finitely many points and factorization through the normalization of the image, and invariance of the genus of a normalization. Layer 12 states the first two; the last two are required in addition. The analytic comparison is excluded by AlgebraicCurves' scope and is taken from ComplexComparisonPartII as cited by GF.5/degree-conventions.

The field finite-étale/Galois equivalence transporting group objects, homomorphisms and pairings, applied to F_p-module schemes and actual G_K-linear isomorphisms. (Its comparison with the scheme instance is IG.0/field-and-torus-comparisons.)

Effective descent and finite-presentation models of elliptic schemes, homomorphisms and torsion isomorphisms, with the agreement locus of two morphisms. review.notes:
Independent review of the eleven-layer design (66 nodes, now 67). Read in full: Bakker–Tsimerman, Annals 184 (2016) 709–744 (SHA-256 verified), the five-page author erratum, Abramovich alg-geom/9609012 and arXiv 1403.7168v1 Proposition 29; BLR §1.2 Proposition 8 (p. 15) and §1.4 Proposition 2 (p. 19) checked in the cleared copy. All eleven baseline declarations were read at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 and are confirmed. The suggested file elaborates with lean-check (only proof-placeholder warnings).

Mathematics verified independently: the replacement systolic witness M_p (exact word identities, M_p≡I mod p, trace 2p²+2, compact trace ratio →27/(4π²) with O(1/p) error for primes to 100003); the T₁×T₁ counterexample to published Proposition 27 (ratio 3p/(p−6)); the negative-reflection cusp example against published Proposition 17 (an ordinary cyclic boundary isogeny with label ratio a, a²=−1, forces m=uv≥p−1); the rotation identity sinh(D/2)=sinh d·|sin(θ/2)|; the Green-identity/coarea derivation of the HV.4 point-ball request and the (z,az) example showing V(t)/a(t) decreases; the Hurwitz bookkeeping, the 7/800 arithmetic, the index/cusp/genus counts and the elementary proper-subgroup index argument.

Corrections made. (1) GF.9: Hecke containment of the classifying map already gives a geometric cyclic isogeny f with f[p]=λΨ, and σ(f)=±f with f[p] invertible and p odd forces σ(f)=f; the design's sentence that no K-isogeny follows from the containment was false. GF.9/geometric-prime-to-p-isogeny and actual-linear-descent now state this, the descent no longer assumes full SL₂ image, characteristic-zero-spread was split (new node GF.9/characteristic-zero-monodromy keeps the monodromy statement over any k), and the end theorem's threshold is any M_N≥max(M_N^geom,5): its closure no longer needs Abramovich, Li–Yau or the congruence spectral gap, which remain targets of GF.8. (2) GF.0/projective-frames duplicated the accepted ModularCurvesPartII:R13.4a/projective-scalar-coarse-quotient (whose uses already cite Bakker–Tsimerman); it is now a comparison adapter fixing the action and component conventions, without its own API, tests or planet. GF.0/hecke-loci now takes T_m, its boundary maps and the ψ(m) pull-push degree from ModularCurvesPartII:R14.1/projective-boundary-hecke-and-degree and adds only H_m and Hecke curves. (3) Twelve bare-stage requests to ModularCurvesPartII and IG.0 were replaced by the exact accepted supplier nodes (R12.1–R14.1 nodes, IG.1/charzero-base-extension, SF.1/finite-group-quotient, SF.1/galois-descent-quasi-projective, SF.0/spreading-out-models, SF.5 nodes, A6/hom-descent-at-full-level, Tau Ceti ModularCurves §2C for φ̂∘φ=[deg φ]); the remaining requests were narrowed to what the suppliers lack, after a clause-by-clause check against the supplier packets and the upstream READMEs (TauCetiRoadmap PRs #913, #852, #850, #849, #848 and main). Upstream SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.17 already states projective finite quotients, recorded in the SF.1 request. Elementary half-plane trigonometry that upstream FuchsianOrbifolds lacks is now requested from HV.0. Unused prerequisites were dropped. (4) 59 of 66 source matches were generic; all were rewritten from the pages. Locators were made precise throughout (57 edited); nine were wrong (the triangle uniformization is in the opening of §3, not §3.1; Lemmas 6 and 10, Proposition 7 and display (2)–(3) sit on pp. 720–722; the reconstruction proofs run to p. 731; the quotient singularities are on p. 742, not p. 743). 30 generic acceptance lines were replaced by node-specific checks and 34 unit-test kinds corrected. (5) GF.0/quotient-branch-locus: stabilizer orders were attached to the wrong strata in the wording; corrected. (6) Source issues: all twenty findings checked at their locators and confirmed, linked to the atlas errata PAPER-BAKKER-TSIMERMAN-16 where already recorded; E15 now affects nothing; new finding E22 (erratum Proposition 4.2 counts each point of overlapping bicusp balls once; the cusp count p^{24δ₃} is missing, harmless for small δ₃). (7) The design's upstream note named the head of a TauCetiRoadmap PR branch as main; corrected. Coverage lists are now per stage.
